finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated directly into the query string. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, for example a boolean or CASE-based blind injection in ORDER BY, or a subquery that reads other tables.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) in list_users_sorted()

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id' takes attacker input with no validation
$sort is concatenated into the SQL string and run via PDO::query(), with no parameterization or allowlist

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, cast or escaping on this path. Prepared statements cannot bind identifiers and none are used here. The sibling function list_users_safe() (line 9-13) does apply an allowlist, but list_users_sorted() does not use it. No authentication or authorization check exists in the file. I did not check whether list_users_sorted() is called from elsewhere, since list.php is the only file in the directory.

verdict.guard_found: none on list_users_sorted(); the allowlist at list.php:10-11 exists only in list_users_safe() and is not used by the vulnerable function
verdict.reason: list.php:5 reads $_GET['sort'] and list.php:6 concatenates it into a PDO::query() ORDER BY with no allowlist, cast or binding, so an anonymous caller can inject SQL (e.g. a CASE/subquery) in SQLite. Caveat: nothing in the directory calls list_users_sorted(), so reachability depends on code outside it.

verdict_facts.reason: list.php:5-6 concatenates raw $_GET['sort'] into the ORDER BY clause of $pdo->query() with no allowlist or parameterization (the allowlist exists only in the separate list_users_safe at list.php:10-11), and nothing in the directory requires authentication, so any HTTP client can inject SQL.
